caption: Figure 1. Learning speed comparison for DQN and the new asynchronous algorithms on five Atari 2600 games. DQN was trained on a single Nvidia K40 GPU while the asynchronous methods were trained using 16 CPU cores. The plots are averaged over 5 runs. In the case of DQN the runs were for different seeds with fixed hyperparameters. For asynchronous methods we average over the best 5 models from 50 experiments with learning rates sampled from LogUniform (10 - 4 , 10 - 2 ) and all other hyperparameters fixed.
description:
This figure is a collection of five line graphs comparing the learning speed of different algorithms on five Atari 2600 games. Each graph shows the average score over training time in hours. The algorithms compared are DQN, 1-step Q, 1-step SARSA, n-step Q, and A3C. The highest performing algorithm varies by game, with A3C often leading, while DQN is consistently the lowest performer across all games.

caption: Figure 2. caption: Figure S5. Comparison of three different optimization methods (Momentum SGD, RMSProp, Shared RMSProp) tested using two different algorithms (Async n -step Q and Async Advantage Actor-Critic) on four different Atari games (Breakout, Beamrider, Seaquest and Space Invaders).
